items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The new musicians that I did not know but had the opportunity to meet were ... Butch Ballard a drummer that Duke had engaged to play the serious drum parts

ctx.x: Duke Ellington was on his first tour of Europe after world war II and it was a delightful pleasure to know that he would be coming to Rome during the time I was there. This was in May and Duke played a theatre for 5 to 6 concerts. It was something for Lily also, because she had never seen or heard of a big band playing jazz. The musicians I knew were Jimmy Hamilton, Sonny Greer, Harry Carney, Ray Nance, Al Killian, Russel Procope, Quinton Jackson, Johnny Hodges, the Duke himself, Don Byas who had been engaged to…

The new musicians that I did not know but had the opportunity to meet were Ernie Royal, a trumpetist, Alvin McCain, a tenor man, Butch Ballard a drummer that Duke had engaged to play the serious drum parts while Sonny featured on certain numbers that called for his showmanship. I didn't know Wendell Marshall, the bass player, but Lily and I went to four concerts and eventually we became acquainted with all the musicians I had not known before and that was the first time that I had heard Duke and his men so many…

Not long after Duke left Rome, Roy Eldridge came for one concert with Benny Goodman. It was a small combo which I did not hear, but I met the drummer whose name was Ed Shaughnessy and we went to the Florida Club to have a drink with he and Roy. They told me that "Toots" Thielemans, the guitar and harmonica player from Belgium was with the group. I knew of "Toots" but had not met him. It was a nice feeling to meet my ole colleague Roy in Rome where we had no idea we would meet when we played together in Teddy…
